correctness.rationale: The source defines H_M as a full finite-dimensional span (p35 Eq4.13) and E(Theta,v) as a linear functional in v (Eq4.14). A8 on p36 states a finite unit maximum of the diagonal second moments over w∈H_M×∂B; E(Theta,c v)=c E(Theta,v) gives second moment c² times the original for any c, so every nontrivial variational moment makes this supremum infinite. The parameter derivatives remain linear in v, hence the first-component discrepancy D_t(v) in Theorem4.3 p46 Eq4.109 is homogeneous and has infinite supremum unless D_t≡0. The proof Lemmas4.1–4.2 explicitly assume ||v||_{1,B}≤1 (p37–38), whereas A10 merely bounds each chosen basis test v_i. The paper A12 also stipulates positive covariance diagonal for all v, including v=0, another related incompatibility. Full relevant source pages 34–48 actually read using authorized institutional extraction. Pure scaling argument covers every c without numerical sampling.

originality.rationale: This is a precise domain inconsistency in the initiating 59-page article, not claimed as a new general functional-analysis lemma. VPINN frameworks with normalized finite tests and dual norms are prior, and mathematical homogeneity is elementary; the nontrivial incremental finding is identifying failure of the particular paper’s A8 and its central variational lazy-training theorem as literally written. No identical erratum was identified in Resultary or inspected source, but later author correction remains possible.
